tagline: One American life, from birth to 25

opening.title: This is {name}.
opening.text:
{name} is about to be born. Over the next 25 years, some of what happens to {obj} will be chosen, some will be luck, and some was settled before {subj} arrived.

The story follows {obj} in the third person. At each turning point, you make the call: first for {poss} family, then for {name}.
opening.nameNote: {Poss} name was drawn at random from the 200 most common names given to babies in the United States in {namesYear}.

letChanceNote: Picks {poss} parents and hometown at random, weighted by how common each is in the US.

profile.notEstimatedNote: Pay during apprenticeship training and military service isn't in the model yet, so those years are left out of the totals.
profile.compareIntro: The same seed, the same hometown, and the same choices wherever they were open, with a different family background. Chance events are the same; how hard they land is not.
profile.leavesOut: This model doesn't assign race or ethnicity, disability, immigration status, or sexual orientation, and gender sets only pronouns. Research shows each of these shapes opportunity in the US. Racial gaps in upward mobility, for example, are large even among children whose parents earned the same income.
